body:
@RomneyDa Not sure if you think of bumping the version number of the @continuedev/config-yaml, but if so, I think it should be set when the merging is done, because any change I do now, will soon become obsolete.

I didn't find any other modifications related to reasoning. Also verified that adding reasoning and reasoningBudgetTokens works with a yaml config like this:
```
  - name: Claude 3.7 Sonnet (thinking)
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-3-7-sonnet-latest
    apiKey: YOUR-API-KEY
    roles:
      - chat
    chatOptions:
      baseSystemMessage: |
        You are intelligent, helpful and an expert developer, who always gives the correct answer and follow instructions.
    defaultCompletionOptions:
      contextLength: 200000
      maxTokens: 32000
      reasoning: true
      reasoningBudgetTokens: 1024
```

Before this modification, I was not able to get reasoning to work with the yaml config, although it was working with the json.

author: fbricon

body:
In the absence of a proper clipboard eventing mechanism (https://github.com/continuedev/continue/commit/449d0b52532e1862d6b8b0eb281de80b535a3232 is too limited) I'd rather prefer a solution where the clipboard content is checked when needed, so no need to register a spy service. So core would send a request to the IDE to fetch the clipboard only when necessary. But I'm not too familiar with the clipboard usage in Continue's codebase, so this solution might have been explored and discarded already.

 I need to look at https://github.com/continuedev/continue/commit/9dd6284b8e4b1dc09b704bc00d5231af9569b6bc in more details, maybe there's a way to simplify this thing after all.

body:
Neat idea, thanks for opening the PR!

I think it would likely make more sense to add this as a boolean option to the params for the HTTP provider: https://docs.continue.dev/customize/context-providers#http

That way it's more of an opt-in behavior.
author: Patrick-Erichsen

body:
I'm glad you like it and thanks for the feedback!

When I just thought about naming for that config prop, it randomly occurred to me that this feature could potentially be used to provide even more local context (path to file that's being edited, selected text). Which is related to [my feedback here](https://discord.com/channels/1108621136150929458/1156679146932535376/1361294827500732448). In that case, I'd call it e.g. `localContext`. From my point of view, this would depend on two things:
- One could argue that it's too much lumped into one thing.
- Were you maybe planning to add the features that I mentioned in that feedback there anyway? (Or are you now) Although... regardless of whether you do, I suppose this kind of information may also be useful to HTTP providers in general.
author: s-h-a-d-o-w

body:
I think the way it's implemented now is fair, and if we find it often used, we could consider a config option. But erring on the side of avoiding new config is usually my preference.

One thing to note is that Model Context Protocol is solving this exact problem with [roots](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/roots). As far as I can tell MCP can do everything that our HttpContextProvider can (with [resources](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/resources)). I'm curious whether you found any limitations, or just had the HttpContextProvider set up before, or maybe hadn't considered MCP? @s-h-a-d-o-w
author: sestinj

body:
> One thing to note is that Model Context Protocol is solving this exact problem with [roots](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/roots). As far as I can tell MCP can do everything that our HttpContextProvider can (with [resources](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/concepts/resources)). I'm curious whether you found any limitations, or just had the HttpContextProvider set up before, or maybe hadn't considered MCP? @s-h-a-d-o-w

I have implemented an MCP server as well. But HttpContextProvider can provide initial context in Chat. Which was my primary goal.

(I actually wasn't aware of `roots` though, that's great to know! That's gonna be helpful. Although—at least based on the docs, you're currently not providing any info there, right?)

body: Hey @uinstinct , I've watched the video a few times but I'm still a bit confused. Why do we need both of the comamnds?
author: Patrick-Erichsen

body:
> Hey @uinstinct , I've watched the video a few times but I'm still a bit confused. Why do we need both of the comamnds?

Sure, I will try to explain. Toggling using command palette with `continue: open settings` is somewhat unintuitive. It opens the chat area when the settings ui is open (despite the given command).
Toggling with the settings button on the gui is intuitive because there is instant feedback between the chat and config page views. User understands we are switching between those 2 views.

author: Patrick-Erichsen

We could also remove other commands present both with an icon and in the command palette (those including settings, view history, new session, open in new window).
Or should we just remove the settings?

body:
@sestinj Before submitting this PR, I was confused and therefore didn't change any other relevant code except the drop-down menu. Actually inline doesn't work as expected, I'm raising the issue now.

1. Does the drop-down menu option value in inline come from `config.modelsByRole.edit`, or from `config.modelsByRole.chat`, or `config.modelsByRole.edit ?? config.modelsByRole.chat` 
(Normally it should be `config.modelsByRole.edit`, and use `config.modelsByRole.chat` if `config.modelsByRole.edit` does not exist, but **streamDiffLines** only uses `config.selectedModelByRole.chat`, 
https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/8057b2ae73dbc49609520dbd4713ba87358b8f9a/core/core.ts#L77-L82
and is the edit role necessarily also the chat role?)

2. Selecting a model in the drop-down menu does not work, it does not change the value of selectedModelByRole because it does not send the `config/updateSelectedModel` message to the core.
So does the IDE need to send a message when a model is selected, or use this code in streamDiffLines?
`
const llm = msg.data.modelTitle ?? config.selectedModelByRole.chat
`
author: lkk214

body:
@lkk214 you're right, it is supposed to be `config.modelsByRole.edit ?? config.modelsByRole.chat`.

Do you want me to merge now and let you make this update in another PR?
author: sestinj

body:
> Selecting a model in the drop-down menu does not work, it does not change the value of selectedModelByRole because it does not send the config/updateSelectedModel message to the core.
So does the IDE need to send a message when a model is selected, or use this code in streamDiffLines?
const llm = msg.data.modelTitle ?? config.selectedModelByRole.chat

Send `config/updateSelectedModel`, or `msg.data.modelTitle ?? config.selectedModelByRole.chat`?

I prefer the latter. I need it for my next PR, otherwise I don't know which selectedModelByRole applies to the selected model and don't want to update the selected model of chat through it, any thoughts on this?

author: coinzz

body:
@coinzz great to hear, thanks a lot for that!

Basically, you need to implement this [interface](https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community/blob/f50abc6062773c82daa76b757ad1bb199ce05b1e/platform/platform-impl/codeinsight-inline/src/com/intellij/codeInsight/inline/completion/InlineCompletionProvider.kt).

A brief overview:
* Implement `isEnabled(event)` to let the platform know whether your provider is applicable in the current context. 
  * The implementation should be fast as it's called on EDT. 
  * Usually, a provider is enabled on `InlineCompletionEvent.DocumentChange` (== a typing in an editor) and `InlineCompletionEvent.DirectCall` (== a user invokes the inline completion by shortcut). 
  * There are also other built-in events. If you lack of the default events, please use `InlineCompletionEvent.ManualCall`. 
  * If the completion of your plugin is disabled by some setting, please return `false` in this case. It's important to let other providers work in case your provider is unavailable.
* Implement `getSuggestion(request)`. 
  * It is called on a background thread, so it may do some heavy stuff/internet access.
  * The result is basically a flow of some elements. If you need to render gray text, please use `InlineCompletionGrayTextElement`
  * There is `InlineCompletionTextElement` to provide colorful suggestions.
  * If you need to jump over a few symbols in the editor (e.g., a suggestion inserts text at several close offsets in the editor), please use `InlineCompletionSkipTextElement`.
  * Please do not create your own implementations of `InlineCompletionElement`. Otherwise, it would not work in the Remote Development setup.
* If you need a custom handling when your suggestion is inserted into the editor, please override `insertHandler`.
* A bonus. There is a native support for the Remote Development setup.

Hey @Patrick-Erichsen 
I dove deeper. I think we will need to replace `sqlite3` package with [`better-sqlite3`](https://github.com/WiseLibs/better-sqlite3) which would be able to accomplish closing connections due to its synchronous nature (and it is also faster than the sqlite3 package).
We have a few instances of sqlite so I don't anticipate any breaking changes. If the team wants to replace with this new package, I can start drafting a PR.

Hmm, were on a bit of a stability push right now so I'd be weary to shake things up too much by swapping out our sqlite lib. 

Mind sharing how you came to the conclusion that we need to do that?
author: Patrick-Erichsen

body:
> Hmm, were on a bit of a stability push right now so I'd be weary to shake things up too much by swapping out our sqlite lib.

Agree. Right now stability is important.

> Mind sharing how you came to the conclusion that we need to do that?

Sure. 
The main problem right now is on closing connections. Sqlite is performing another transaction and hence is unable to close the connection. Had this been synchronous, we would be sure that the previous sqlite transaction was complete. Due to node-sqlite's asynchronous nature the connection seems to perform operations while we are closing it.

<details>
<summary>small history how can i came to this conclusion</summary>

The main problem that we are getting during testing (in both local and actions) is that connections are not closing after tests. This is could be due to:
a) unfinalized statements
b) memory leak issue
I inspected the first case multiple times to check for such statements and we are finalizing all prepare statements.
We are even [committing/rolling back unfinished transactions](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/a4f05d13d6438a50467b1c050f60c2c655b06fa1/core/indexing/refreshIndex.ts/#L112-L120).
The second case is some operation is underway while we are closing it. This could be due to multiple reasons like jest not resetting modules properly between tests or incomplete test isolation or statements that are persisting across tests. Upon searching ways to avoid this, I came across better-sqlite3.
</details>

I can give better-sqlite3 a try in a Proof-of-Concept.

body:
@sestinj Thank you for the feedback, agreed that it's best to avoid such hyper-specific logic (I didn't create such a chat template as I was trying to to keep things consistent with codestral being assigned the 'none' template in `core/llm/autodetect.ts`–as it's not needed when using the Mistral messages API, but now realize that was a better approach anyway.)
I just opened a [PR](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/5523) containing a 'codestral' template in `core/llm/templates/chat.ts`

> Also, I notice that we are only sending the last message to the model in _streamChat—do you know whether this is something we will be able to update in the near future, or is this a limitation of WatsonX?

The entire conversation is actually getting passed in this last 'message' (but the logic is hidden in the `_complete` function due to the original implementation). I just opened a [PR](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/5522) with the integration of the watsonx Chat API, in which this part of the code is refactored.

body:
The minimal python SSE server to test is this:

```
# requirements.txt
# Server
fastapi==0.115.4
uvicorn~=0.34
# MCP
mcp[cli]~=1.8.0
```

```python
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
from mcp.server.fastmcp.prompts import base
from starlette.applications import Starlette
from starlette.routing import Host, Mount

mcp = FastMCP("My App")


# Add an addition tool
@mcp.tool()
def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    """Add two numbers"""
    return a + b


@mcp.prompt()
def review_code(code: str) -> str:
    """Review code prompt"""
    return f"Please review this code:\n\n{code}"


@mcp.prompt()
def debug_error(error: str) -> list[base.Message]:
    """Debug error prompt"""
    return [
        base.UserMessage("I'm seeing this error:"),
        base.UserMessage(error),
        base.AssistantMessage("I'll help debug that. What have you tried so far?"),
    ]


@mcp.resource("greeting://{name}")
def get_greeting(name: str) -> str:
    """Get a personalized greeting"""
    return f"Hello, {name}!"


# Mount the SSE server to the existing ASGI server
app = Starlette(
    routes=[
        Mount("/", app=mcp.sse_app()),
    ]
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn

    uvicorn.run(
        "minimal:app", host="127.0.0.1", port=8000, log_level="debug", reload=True
    )
```

```yaml
mcpServers:
  - name: Debug Local Minimal MCP Python
    type: sse
    url: http://127.0.0.1:8000/sse
```

body:
Hey @chezsmithy , thanks for the PR!

Chatted this over with @sestinj this morning - we both agreed that the chat/agent system messages are a great addition, but the tool calling in Chat mode we'd like to avoid. I can see the value in having the subset of tools available in Chat, but the problem is that exposing these tools makes the models way too eager to use tools instead of just answering questions directly, which is the intended behavior for Chat. E.g. I tried to ask a simple question with 3.7 Sonnet and instead it searched my codebase, couldn't find the answer, then searched the web, etc

With that being said, a few points of feedback on the system message updates:
- Can we update the rule title in the GUI so that instead of always `Default chat system message`, it says `Default agent system message` when in agent mode?
- In general I think the agent system message could be shortened a bit
- The "lazy edits" part of both sys msgs should be pulled out into a variable and reused in both to make sure they use the same instructions for this
- Chat prompt should have clearer instructions that the user can use the "Apply" button (I was told to copy/paste when asking for an edit, when I should be told to use the Apply button)

body:
So aside from autoindent there's a bigger problem, despite LLMs generally being smarter than intellisense, there are points when there's not enough "there, there" for it to anticipate what the user wants. In those cases, intellisense still outshines the LLM because it puts what to do next in the user's hands.

So I have a new idea which I plan to experiment with soon. Rather than inhibit the suggestion widget until the LLM is ready, allow it to show at any point, but add a place holder item to the top of it that represents the LLMs (pending) response.

In this way we shouldn't need hacks that break autoindent, we don't hide the suggestion widget in cases the user actually would prefer it and we still provide way for the user to take control while they wait.

I'll see if I can whip this branch into something that meshes with that workflow.  See also some small quick wins Owen and Keerthana did in https://github.com/Granite-Code/continue-for-granite/pull/42 . When I update this branch i'll make sure it's on top of those changes.

body:
Figured it out! 🥳
We do not want to modify nodes which are not markdown tables. So [added an early return](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/5560/commits/0a498817665dcf31e3fd862039ae745b5c005221).

Previous approach was removing the space between the paragraph's text nodes due to the [buffer addition logic](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/5560/files#diff-653dd774a4545a99f8cebf78bcbb6c3341c846abec11a60c1ee1a5cc0e06041aR26-R29). This was because remark does not treat line breaks as nodes (or we need to make another remark plugin).
I figured it out by intentionally [failing the test](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/actions/runs/15134172666/job/42542137401) on main branch code and comparing the screenshots. The only difference was in line breaks.

body:
Actually this test checks exactly access by file url: primary difference from absolute path test is `pathToFileURL` call. It converts usual file path (`urlFilePath`) to `file://` URL and then this string (`fileUrl`) is used in primary part of test. 

And as `pathToFileURL` is used in the rest of the extension to create file URLs from usual paths, this test covers all cases of local file URLs usage in the extension (of course, except URLs entered by users).

File content is changed just in case to protect against confusing variables with absolute path test. It does not affect on test logic itself.

And of course, I have checked, that this test really works: I have reverted my first commit and the test became failed.

body:
Another thought.

Maybe we have adaptive cancel. 

If you cancel a thinking call or LLM request after a user message, it rolls to the last user message.

If you cancel during a tools call it only cancels the call but doesn't roll back. Perhaps if a tools call has occurred since the last user message we never allow roll back, only cancelling the next tool call.

body:
@RomneyDa I want to solve for the following:

Today using AWS bedrock as a back end hitting the cancel button result in a non presumable session about 70% of the time. The user has to start a new session to recover loosing all context.

* Cancelled thinking removes orphaned tags that break the AWS converse API.
* Cancelled tool calls always have an added tool result to not break the AWS converse API and the LLM is fully aware of tool status.
* Cancelled assistant messages that might be truncated are removed.
* Cancelling tools like terminal or apply leave you in an expected consistent state.
* The LLM is aware that cancellation was triggered so it stops and asks for further instructions before proceeding with any tasks.

Where I am at:

* thinking and assistant messages are cleaned up.
* orphaned tool call and results are handled in the history. However, I've noted a few edge cases where I still get orphaned results breaking the ability to resume when I hit the cancel button right at the start of tool calls. 
* Cancelling the terminal is wired up but the UI needs work.
* Writing the assistant message at the end of the cancellation can end with some overwrite in the UI.
* Cancelling the apply/edit tool needs your fixes to allow cancellation to arrive at a consistent state.
* Should solve for rejecting all edits on cancel.

Hope this helps? - S.
author: chezsmithy

body: @chezsmithy thanks for this in depth feedback, I think with all these points we're close to understanding the full solution. I'll be bumping tool architecture fixes this week, will make sure to rope you in if you're available, we will likely be able to reuse most of this

author: RomneyDa

body: I think agent mode is fantastic and is very powerful. It gives a kinda wow moment for users when they first use it. Currently, it feels hidden (especially on 13 inch screens as you only have the icon with a small drop down arrow). Users have to actively to go look through the modes to find agent mode, which they may not even know exists. I think there's a similar issue with tool permissions but that's harder to solve. Starting off in agent mode will allow users to get to the most powerful version of continue quicker leading a better experience.
author: gs-pal

body: @gs-pal thinking about removing edit mode from the dropdown and making agent more of toggle that says "Agent" to make it clearer. Would that be an improvement?
author: RomneyDa

body: Maybe we should have something show up for first time users to explain the modes? I've seen a similar lack of agent mode use in our user base until we've done showcases and training. Now they are so excited.
author: chezsmithy

body: We added something in the onboarding to call out agent mode, which is a good first step, but I agree we could do more. Agent mode as default soon perhaps, something else in the meantime
author: sestinj

body: I think the toggle is a great idea. Personally, I don't think edit mode is useful anymore so I'd agree with removing it.
author: gs-pal

body: Thanks all for the input here. Let's look into moving Edit out of the "modes"/toggling in the near future and make agent more obvious by having a toggle that shows agent on or off, rather than a selector that shows the _current_ mode. Then, maybe we can try having agent on as default as well. Will close this for now.

Other than the `<important_rules>`, is there any way to review this is a an AGENT interaction and not a CHAT action? I feel like you could deduce AGENT mode from the inclusion of Tools in the log data, but otherwise there is no classification about this being an AGENT interaction and not a normal CHAT interaction type? With the existing schemas available, I always assumed that we would introduce a new pair of data schemas like `agentInteraction` and `agentOutcome` or similar...

It's logical to think that the AGENT features would be a separate namespace and not overloaded in the existing CHAT data space. I worry this will be hard to disambiguate the utilization of AGENT mode compared to CHAT. Seems like there are ideas on how this might change over time from @Patrick-Erichsen and @RomneyDa

author: sestinj

body:
@sestinj agreed that the model can somewhat infer new file contents based on changes. This is for case of only some or none of the diffs being accepted. Currently if you reject diffs Agent mode continues on as if the edits were all accepted. This is a heuristic solution that might be a bit token expensive but is a safe start and works well with smoke testing.

Reasoning for this approach came from convo with @Patrick-Erichsen, we landed on these reasons
- We could add diff info to apply state and feed it back to the model, but it would be a bigger change and has some problems
   - Apply state doesn't contain diff info which is a non trivial add 
   - even if it did the model wouldn't confidently be able to correlate it's change suggestions (lazy) to diffs (apply model)
   - users can edit diffs before accepting/rejecting, which complicates things

One improvement would be if all rejected don't send new file contents just say user rejected try something else. 

Another improvement would be to only send the updated range, e.g. beginning of first diff to end of last diff or similar to save tokens on huge files. 

Finally we could add some meta comments like of not all diffs were accepted add a cautionary: "here is the file after changes, note that the user did not accept all changes" or similar

Think any of these are important before merging or thoughts on different approaches?

body:
@uinstinct nice improvements, I think this is closer but still have some thoughts.
I think we don't need tool output to be associated with args, i.e. it shouldn't say "show/hide args" if it's also going to show/hide output. Args _could_ be nested within a toggleable that by default only shows context items, but probably not vice versa. ContextItem has a `hidden` property that can be used to filter context items. If any context items are not hidden, then it should just show them in a collapsible div (like toggle div). If non are not hidden, then it should not show anything and not be collapsible. That is
- The previous "Simple" tools can be clickable so that they show the tool output below where the args would pop down if they have non-hidden ContextItems
- Custom tool call divs like Edit or Terminal can have their context items incorporated case by case, e.g. terminal already has custom streaming output logic, but edit tool could have context items shown below (results of edit e.g. https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/5821)

Great tests btw

Somewhat rambling, let me know if you have any questions about this or ideas for other approaches

body:
@AfterStories thanks for the bump

@uinstinct checking in, some thoughts/review
1. Virtual file is great for tool output
2. Agreed that SimpleToolCallUI and ToolCallDiv should be merged, but let's do it in a way that doesn't effect the simple tool calls as much - the UI is fundamentally different in that the simple tool call will show the chevron that can dropdown Tool Output, while the non-simple ones (edit, terminal, etc.) should not have a chevron, and always show output. Let's merge the components but keep that simple chevron functionality
3. Talking with @Patrick-Erichsen today we do think that putting the args in a modal (same args button) as in @AfterStories feedback makes sense, and the tool output could also be shown in that modal but at least would be shown in context item peeks in chat still

So in summary
- args just shows a modal with args
- output always shows below as context item peek, toggleable chevron look for "simple" tools, and shown in custom ways for "non-simple" tools, e.g. terminal streams in, edit always shows context item peek (nothing for now since no output).

On the flip side I can also see having it in `<Chat />` being noisy in a different way, so if we do keep it in the notch my only feedback is on copy.

- `Eject from trial` -> `Exit Trial`
- `Using free trial` -> `Free Trial usage`
- `You are currently using the free trial` -> `Free Trial of the Models Add-On`
- Subtext for the above title (adapted from https://docs.continue.dev/hub/governance/pricing#models-add-on)

body: @RomneyDa I have the feeling that `maxDepth` requires less thinking and is safer as you won't explicitly know how many pages will be indexed by each glob, don't you think ?
author: vincentkelleher

body: we're thinking also about adding a `maxPages` to give a more direct limit, but I think people generally either want to index all docs that match a pattern (with a hard limit perhaps). `maxDepth` doesn't create any hard limit, it could yield tens of thousands of pages in somewhat edge casey scenarios
author: RomneyDa

body:
would `maxPages` and `useLocalCrawling` be sufficient?
The other issue with maxDepth is it's not super clear how it works, i.e. as a dev I can't keep a 3-link-deep map of the docs pages I want in my head
author: RomneyDa

body:
It's true that there are clearly two types of limits:
- hard limits with `maxPages`
- soft limits with `maxDepth`, `allowList` and `blockList`

Usually having a max depth of 1 seems like a reasonable case as you want everything directly linked to the subject of the page, doing more than 1 or 2 would directly bring you to indexing the whole website in most cases IMHO. I also think that having an allow or block list would be about the same, if not worse, than a max depth over 1 as you will have to clearly know the sitemap.

Having a maximum number of pages would be a good guard-rail to avoid using too many hardware resources, that seems like a good feature :+1: 

I would go for `useLocalCrawling`, `maxDepth` and `maxPages` :innocent:
author: vincentkelleher

body: @vincentkelleher appreciate the feedback! Do you currently have cases for which you set maxDepth > 1?
author: RomneyDa

body: @RomneyDa I don't have any in mind right now :thinking:
author: vincentkelleher

body: After running by team opened a new PR to remove maxDepth for YAML, opened a ticket to add maxPages/allow/block list or similar to replace. Will leave useLocalCrawling. Thanks for the contribution!

body:
Hi @drocko , apologies for the delay here, I thought I had already reviewed this.

I'm a bit confused by what "Composition Order Flow" is supposed to mean though, even after reading the issue and viewing that image.

Is the goal here to try to clarify how the context window is filled?
author: Patrick-Erichsen

body:
Hi @Patrick-Erichsen, no worries at all about the delay, and sorry if my diagram caused any confusion!

Yes, my goal was to clarify how the context window was filled aka the "Composition Order" defined by [lisyoen](https://github.com/lisyoen) in the [ original issue](https://github.com/continuedev/continue/issues/5112). Thought it would be a good first issue for me to try and tackle!

And about that diagram - I’m not sure if it’s a bug but I noticed the newest message sometimes doesn’t show up in the console logs, which made it a bit confusing to determine the actual composition order. My earlier notes and diagram were an attempt to explain that behavior, but they may have ended up making things more confusing instead.
author: drocko

body:
Got it - I appreciate the contribution but I don't think we really have anywhere good to put this in the docs right now. It isn't specifically related to the `prompts.md` file you added it to since that is specifically about prompt files, this "composition flow" is moreso about how we construct user messages, which is a bit too in the weed for the docs.

Closing the issue out with that in mind, but if you're looking for a good first issue I think this might be a good one: https://github.com/continuedev/continue/issues/6222
author: Patrick-Erichsen

body: Eventually I could see this going into some sort of "Context management" doc however so I'll keep it in mind 👍

body:
> @G81192 can you provide more information about this approach? I'm thinking maybe it shouldn't be called "getOrOpen" if the create functionality is added. Maybe we could call it getOrCreate or something, or make the flow more clear. I want to make sure we're not creating files when we shouldn't

@RomneyDa Thank you for the reply.

The issue I'm encountering is that, with the current unmodified code, when I try to create a new file generated by the LLM by clicking create file, nothing happens. Instead, the file currently open in the IDEA window gets modified.

After looking into the code, I found that the getOrOpenEditor method returns the currently selected file as the editor when the target file does not exist. However, in my case, I need to create a new file — and since it doesn’t exist yet, this results in an error.
Example:

1. I want to create the file:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6bfde522-fafb-4de1-9634-a21a32efe850)

2. When I click create file, the currently open file in the IDEA window gets modified instead, which leads to an error:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c034dcd-c72e-4b2b-ac7b-fdd5e1dc5047)

3.  This is the expected behavior I want to achieve:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/103de924-8c3d-4b30-889f-2e8a65b8ae8d)

This PR is intended to fix this issue. If anything is unclear, I’m happy to provide more details.

body:
Thanks @jpoly1219, that's a great point.

The key difference is that this new shortcut works **while automatic suggestions are still enabled**, offering a "best of both worlds" experience.

It provides immediate value by allowing users to:
1.  Manually force a request if one is missed due to a slow model or network.
2.  Re-trigger a suggestion after accidentally dismissing it.

It also could potentially serve as a foundation for future PR, specifically allowing user to re-trigger autocompletes with slight variation in temperature or seed, essentially a "re-roll" workflow allowing the user to quickly cycle through  different suggestions.

body:
Yes, so the bulk of the issue is around thinking tags, but specifically how OpenAI-compatible models such as Qwen3 send them. Sometimes they send them in a streaming format which Continue already handles, but other times they send the entire message in one chunk, which will look something like:

```
<think>Okay, I am an AI model and I am thinking about something</think>

Hello user, here is the message that I am displaying to you.
```

And these can also have tool calls attached in the same message. Continue currently doesn't support this non-streaming message format, so this change adds support for it.
author: shssoichiro

body:
Thanks, I've updated the code to place the `think` block messages into the `reasoning` section of the previous message, as we do elsewhere. It was easier to keep the overall structure of the PR, where we parse full blocks first, due to the different handling required for splitting them.

as a note, I ran into difficulties with manual retesting due to errors related to `Cannot find module '@continuedev/openai-adapters'` while attempting to update dependencies. I'm not sure if that is an issue with my environment or with current `main`, but it seems unrelated to the code affected by this PR.

body: What would be a good way to check for this? Looking at the `ContextProviderDescription`, it seems like the properties there would typically always be the same given that we are always looking at the "codebase" provider.
author: shssoichiro

body: @shssoichiro you are right that changes in `nRetrieve` and `nFinal` and `useReranking` (the only codebase params) should not trigger a refresh. I just mean that the equality expression `codebaseProvider1 === codebaseProvider2` will always evaluate to false, because they are objects that are created with each config reload.

body: Thanks, that makes sense. In that case it probably makes sense to remove that check and just check if the embed provider has changed. I've done that and fixed the merge conflicts.

body:
Seems for best efficient cost/cache ratio, Apply/Edit models better to disable cacheConversations, because apply/edit does not include history. while it make sense, i not sure why rules / system messages stripped out as well (i would prefer to include them to ensure that during edit/apply AI follow the same guidelines as during conversation), but the main point need to disable conersation caching for Edit/Apply to not waste $$$ and pay just for vanilla costs, with caching single input message we literally wasting x1.25 or x2.0 depends on cache type which written to cache but never used after since each edit/apply a new mini-session. 

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20756086-2354-4891-b721-6d35bae3dc32)


In any case i think i did the best from what i can to achieve best caching logic and support Anthropic extended ttl. It works perfect. Small issue with 1h ttl that it has strictly limited TTL and not using LRU style, so its invalidation will always happen after 1hour. It still good option anyway. I have idea maybe to implement sort of "ping" where run timer after last message and automatically send context +ping which will cost few tokens only but will refresh 5min ttl. The problem here it needs more testing and investigation about how long we can keep 5min TTL using ping approach and also have some fail-safe feature to not abuse anthropic functionality where user can forgot to close session and ping can stay for hours and days. So this is only idea.

Also code tested against current main branch with v1.1.56 of plugin. unfortunately i cant do CLA from another account, so maybe it easier to create new PR with rebased from current main and without leftish committers :D

Thanks for the quick fixes! I didn't see any info on model support for tool calling on that doc page but I do here: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing

However I don't see any info on `deepseek-coder` either on that page, or anywhere else on the internet. Can you confirm you've tried this PR our with `deepseek-coder` locally and that it was supported?

If so this is good to merge 👍
author: Patrick-Erichsen

body: In DeepSeek-V2.5, deepseek merged the DeepSeek-V2-Chat and DeepSeek-Coder-V2 models. At the same time, the API interface is forward compatible, and users can access the new model through deepseek-coder or deepseek-chat. As for the latest DeepSeek-V3, although deepseek does not say in the document that the latest model can be accessed through deepseek-coder, I have no problem specifying the model as deepseek-coder in the local configuration file. I am not sure whether deepseek-coder will be supported in the future, so I will remove it.

body:
@chezsmithy will close this for now, partly because +1 to your comment about moving to search and replace.

My other thought is that I think most rules typically should not be included in an apply prompt, since the apply prompt is only supposed to take existing code and apply changes to it, and rules could often confuse this. In the cases you described, I wonder if updating the apply prompt to nudge it to ensure the formatting of the _changes_ takes priority over existing formatting would solve it. E.g. if the changes (made with rules in mind) include the proper fenced codeblocks, the new code should as well. Or to add a boolean rule property `isApplyRule` or something and only include those in apply. I could see it going either way and sounds like including rules did fix it for you in some cases but I'd lean towards leaving rules out and making the apply. 

If needed, you can add an apply prompt using `promptTemplates.apply` to fix your specific issue.

I have it on my list to see if I can prevent removal of comments with this approach, since it's an apply-specific issue.

Let me know if you have any other thoughts on this!

body: This might be a better topic for discord, but I'm curious in your vision for applies. If search and replace were to fail for example how would it fail over to other approaches? Curious.
author: chezsmithy

body: It seems like the solution would be to put the lazy edit instructions into the edit file tool
author: sestinj

body:
And vision for applies follows two different paths:
1. (for the models that can't find and replace yet) we continue to encourage the usual
2. (for the models that can, which is mostly claude right now) we move entirely toward find / replace, except have a robust system of fallbacks. Right now it includes various matching algorithms at various levels of fuzziness. in the future it may include just passing off to a language model. But we think we can get failure rates so low that is doesn't matter

Obviously going to need a bit of feedback from folks as we work on improving this—it will need real-world usage

Thanks for the heads up here @chezsmithy ! I'll postpone merging this til we get https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/6604 merged.

Doesn't seem like things should conflict too much here, I'll just update the logic in the middleware to check for our new array of tool states instead of a singular state. Let me know your thoughts however!
author: Patrick-Erichsen

body: @Patrick-Erichsen totally agree. Should be really easy to adapt to the middleware.
author: chezsmithy

body: Thanks for the additional review @RomneyDa ! Fixed the bug with `` incorrectly rendering. The gap on multiple codeblocks was due to some unnecessary padding, stripped that out as well. Also had accidentally removed our specific rendering for search/replace, added that back. > Pending tool bar looks funny with ls tool: - Agreed but I think we just need a better name for it. Maybe `List files`? > "pause" feels off to me, what was the thought on changing? - No hard logic haha, "Cancel" just felt a bit destructive to me vs "Pause" implies the ability to resume. I've seen "Stop" used in other tools, assuming with similar logic.
author: Patrick-Erichsen

body:
@uinstinct reverting the commit for now, but it would still be nice to have the original feature that you were trying to do here, so might be worth a second shot! 

FWIW, here's what Claude 4 had to say about the issue, seems like it might not be possible if this is true:

```
The problem is that the postDebugTask is set to "Terminate All Tasks" which terminates all tasks when the debug session ends. However, when you reload the debug window (as opposed to fully stopping it), VS Code is treating this as the debug session ending and triggering the postDebugTask.

Let me check if there's a way to distinguish between a reload and a full stop in VS Code's debug configuration, or if we need to modify the approach.

Looking at the current configuration:

The postDebugTask is set to "Terminate All Tasks"
The "Terminate All Tasks" task uses workbench.action.tasks.terminate with terminateAll argument
This terminates ALL tasks, but apparently one task (npm run esbuild-notify) survives
The issue is that VS Code doesn't distinguish between a reload and a stop when it comes to postDebugTask. Both actions trigger the post-debug task.
```

body: @chezsmithy most providers handle the abort 499 code gracefully, whether in streamSse or explicitly. Maybe Bedrock is missing this handling?
author: RomneyDa

body:
>can only issue one set of calls at a time before an abort occurs and I have to manually request the chat should continue

Just to clarify, what do you mean by one set of calls at a time in this context?
author: RomneyDa

body:
@RomneyDa so what I see is the error is getting caught here: https://github.com/continuedev/continue/blob/536f0065d2f29923ddc7d7a31c0cd80f25531f72/core/llm/llms/Bedrock.ts#L263

But the error isn't related to Bedrock, the error is related to the abortSignal getting aborted which causes the streaming to end.

The pattern I see causing the issue is:

1. Ask the LLM to update a file.
2. The tool call occurs.
3. The file updated succeeds using the new search and replace feature.
4. The toolCall returns and sends the results back to the LLM.
5. An abort occurs caught at the line above.

OR

1. Ask the LLM to run tests.
2. The tool call occurs.
3. The tool call succeeds super quickly running the terminal command.
4. The toolCall returns and sends the resutls back to the LLM.
5. An abort occurs caught at the line above.

I've also observed that periodically the assistent reponse from the toolCall becaomes garbled and is rendered out of order in the chat window.

I'm thinking its a race condition that's being uncovered by the performance of the local tool calling. (guessing...)

body: This might be totally fine, but having spent a bunch of time with using this cleanup method I'm curious if we need to make this cleanup more model and provider specific so we don't run the risk of breaking other models and providers which might have different expectations. For example, the AWS Bedrock Converse API is super picky about having perfectly matched tool and reasoning messages. This might not be the case for other providers and models. Thoughts?
author: chezsmithy

body:
> This might be totally fine, but having spent a bunch of time with using this cleanup method I'm curious if we need to make this cleanup more model and provider specific so we don't run the risk of breaking other models and providers which might have different expectations. For example, the AWS Bedrock Converse API is super picky about having perfectly matched tool and reasoning messages. This might not be the case for other providers and models. Thoughts?

Totally agree, different model and provider needs a way to override the default method. It might need another PR to do this. :)

In this PR, the existing code is conflict with `findCurrentToolCall` which expect the message contains tool call must be the last one. So I guess this PR is safe and won't break existing good behaviours?

body: @dan0v can you share more about the workflows that make this important to you? So far as I understand this was a purposeful simplification of prompting. I think we would be happy to revert, but only if there are compelling benefits
author: sestinj

body:
@sestinj For any tool which reads or modifies the codebase, such information is crucial in order to properly identify what code the user is querying. It is also counter-intuitive that in the UI, it looks to the user as if the code snippet which is provided to the model includes the line number information, since it is displayed above the code snippet, when that is no longer the case. The alternative for any tool trying to interact with code based on user queries is to rely on the file path (which is still included in the request) and do a string comparison of the whole file to hope for one of many possible matches on the code snippet. That is a terrible option, when the simple solution of providing that contextual information already existed previously and worked well.

If a similar simplification vein were further pursued, the file path could also be removed from the request, but I would also not recommend such a move, as it would break even more tooling.

In terms of cost/benefit, very little is gained by the removal (I don't know exactly what, if anything to be honest), but existing workflows like my own will be broken by it. The additional context provided in the description is minimal, so won't be consuming a relevant portion of the available tokens and should just be included again as before in my opinion. 

See xkcd-1172 -- I would say my use-case is less niche 😄 :

![xkcd-1172](https://imgs.xkcd.com/comics/workflow_2x.png)
author: dan0v

body:
Fair enough! @RomneyDa I want to check first with you to make sure there wasn't an important reason for this changing. PR where it changed is here: https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/6264

If it looks fine to you, go ahead and merge

I think some of the e2e tests have a valid failure here.

But, I believe at least for `cmd + i` the current behavior is to insert at the cursor location rather than add the line as context. I think this would also break the ability to toggle open/close the sidebar using `cmd + L`.

Is your main thought here that Copilot behaves in the way you showed in that video? 

cc @sestinj for a second opinion on behavior.

body:
Chatted this over with @sestinj 
- We'd like to preserve the `cmd + L` sidebar toggling behavior
- We'd like to preserve `cmd + I` insert behavior, but only on empty lines.

With that in mind, could we scope the update to basically be "if the user pressed `cmd + I` on a line with any characters, the entire line is added to context` ?
author: Patrick-Erichsen

body:
So from what I can see, the existing Cmd+L behavior is to show the webview if hidden, and focus the cursor there. Not sure it's accurate to call it toggle, since another Cmd+L doesn't hide it, but the webview is unfocused.

I can look into reducing the scope of Cmd+I, I'll see if it works

body:
Hey :wave: @aaudin90, apologies for not merging right away, but I was tied up with other priorities. I’ve reviewed your changes, but I’m at bit resistant to merge them because I don’t quite understand the value they bring.

Let me first briefly describe what’s possible right now (on `main` in the context of debugging):

* If you're using Ultimate, you don't need anything else. You don’t need VS Code. Just run the compound run configuration called `Run Continue` in debug mode, and you can set breakpoints both in the Kotlin extension and in the TypeScript server.
* If you're using Community Edition, you can’t debug TypeScript and need to use another IDE like VS Code. For Kotlin, you run `Run Extension` in debug mode in IntelliJ, and for TypeScript, you launch Core + GUI in debug mode in VS Code.

Your changes don’t seem to improve either of these scenarios.

Also, I have a follow-up questions:

> Automatically rebuilds the binary before each session via the new binary:rebuild task, ensuring the debugger always runs the latest code.

This shouldn’t be necessary. Launching `Core Binary` task in VS Code by default compiles the code and everything starts without a "binary". A server is started on port `3000` and communication happens over TCP. That’s why the run configuration in IntelliJ has an extra `USE_TCP=true` argument.

> Sets development-specific environment variables so the binary behaves the same way it does when launched by the Extension.

Can you please point out which environment variables you’re referring to? The new `Core Binary (Debug)` config seems identical to `Core Binary` + extra `binary:rebuild`.

To sum up, could you please elaborate more on what exactly your changes do and what problem they solve? (Note: I’d really like to understand your perspective, and it's possible that, since I'm mainly working with IntelliJ, I'm simply not aware of certain pain points :wink:)

> I might be misunderstanding this, but shouldn't the chunking function chunk the document to within max chunk size? Wondering if there's a bug with the chunky algorithm, and filtering is a band-aid?

It is in fact a band-aid, there as a fallback in case somehow the main chunker fails to properly get below the maxChunkSize. Should this happen? Ideally, no. But if it does there's no reason not to filter to avoid worse problems.

I will say @tingwai it might be useful to also test the function that does the chunking _before_ the filtering. body: **Note about testing**: I could not fully verify whether the requests actually go through the Burp proxy. Even though I imported the proxy certificate at the system level as trusted (into the OS Trusted Store) and additionally provided the certificate via `requestOptions.caBundlePath` for my local config, I can only see part of the decrypted requests. For some reason, certain requests return an enigmatic `Invalid URL` (but without an actual URL :smile:) in the JCEF logs, and I haven't been able to determine the cause. There's no trace of this in the Continue or JCEF source code, and honestly, I’ve already spent so much time on this that I think it can be merged as-is. Since the way the proxy is applied is so trivial, I’m very confident that these changes should work because it’s transparent enough that no changes were needed in the Continue binary code (it's just env vars).

body:
Hi @Patrick-Erichsen,

I've investigated the lint/build errors you mentioned. The issues are not coming from the changes in this PR, but from missing dependencies and TypeScript configuration problems in the main branch.

✅ This PR's files are clean:
# The modified files pass all checks:
cd gui
npx eslint src/components/mainInput/Lump/sections/docs/DocsSection.tsx  # ✓ Passes
npx prettier --check src/components/mainInput/Lump/sections/docs/DocsSection*.tsx  # ✓ Passes

❌ The build errors are from missing dependencies:
All TypeScript errors are in node_modules/@continuedev/core/ (32+ errors), caused by:
•  Missing packages: @continuedev/fetch, @continuedev/llm-info
•  Missing type definitions: @types/jsdom, @types/plist, etc.
•  TypeScript config issues (ES5 target but using ES2015+ features, missing esModuleInterop)

None of these errors are in the files modified by this PR.

body:
@RomneyDa in my debugging for say AWS Bedrock with Sonnet. I noticed that the System Message doesn't include any of the tool definitions as it's native tool use, but then in the tools array passed to the model, the tool description is just the description field and not the systemMessageDescription. Thus the model gets a list of tools, with a very basic agent system message and is left to figure out how to use the tools from the shape of the payloads and a VERY basic tool description. This results in the model using the tools very poorly. Does that make sense?

This fix, re-introduces what would have been in the decription back to the tools array description field fixing tools use for native tools using models.
author: chezsmithy

body:
> @RomneyDa in my debugging for say AWS Bedrock with Sonnet. I noticed that the System Message doesn't include any of the tool definitions as it's native tool use, but then in the tools array passed to the model, the tool description is just the description field and not the systemMessageDescription. Thus the model gets a list of tools, with a very basic agent system message and is left to figure out how to use the tools from the shape of the payloads and a VERY basic tool description. This results in the model using the tools very poorly. Does that make sense?

The system message description is brief blurb + an example of calling the tool using system message tools, e.g. 
```tool
TOOL_NAME: read_file
BEGIN_ARG: filepath
test.js
END_ARG
```

It doesn't apply for native tools, it's mostly duplicate. In many cases, it's more concise. If there is information missing from the normal tool description which is in the system message description, we should add it to the normal tool description.

The issues I've found that led to wanting this tab more visible are indeed related to codebase indexing errors. The most frequent being that the codebase indexing will fail when VSCode initially loads (the common error seems to be `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'signal')`), so I have to visit the Indexing tab, see that often there is an error, and click Re-index, and then it works. May I ask why the codebase indexing overall is being deprecated? I know that is outside the scope of this ticket, but I'm curious as it seems like a useful feature.

body:
I'm still trying to understand why these tests are failing. So far, I've identified two issues:

* This experimental inline completion API crashes for some reason when runIdeForUiTests is used. From what I understand, the coroutine library isn't built-in in 2023.3 ([source](https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/using-kotlin.html#coroutinesLibraries)), and even though I added it as explicit dependency, I'm still getting errors (like class not found). I decided to try bumping the platform version to 2024.1, and that **resolved** the problem (the API is stable starting from that version). If I manage to narrow down the number of issues, I'll try reverting back to 2023.3.
* There was a problem with the XPath selector in Autocomplete test. Turns out the GUI has changed with platform version update and the path was invalid. This is fixed now.

Even with those fixes, the completion still doesn't show up. It behaves in a specific way, because during UI tests we enable an environment variable that points to a test config (it's `src/test/kotlin/com/github/continuedev/continueintellijextension/e2e/test-continue/config.json`). That config includes a "test" model responsible for completion on specific input. For some reason, this mechanism stopped working. Still debugging it. :thinking:

> When I try to launch this state of the PR, I get the error, that the kotlin version is too low. When I try to upgrade it to 2.0.0, I get several other compiler errors. How does this work for you?

Hey @coinzz, it should be fixed now (https://github.com/continuedev/continue/pull/6947/commits/e6b5335ae367e02be7dd7b5ce9324aac203299f4). We were overriding the platform version in our plugin run configuration, which was automatically used when you ran `./gradlew runIde` / `Run Extension` / `Run Continue`.

body: @shssoichiro I think a nice implementation would be to open a virtual file in the IDE listing all the URLs, rather than having a massive tooltip. I originally made a tooltip and then moved it to the DocsDetailsDialog, which was later hidden because it was a bit noisy in the UI. Thoughts on virtual file approach?
author: RomneyDa

body:
I took a look at the `DocsDetailsDialog`, the big difference seems to be that it is listing the indexed content alongside each chunk. How useful do you think that would end up being other than for debugging? Currently the pages in the list are clickable, so the user can open them in the browser.

I think if we are following the tooltip approach, just showing the pages list feels a lot cleaner, but if we move to a virtual file approach then that would be better for showing the indexed content alongside as in the `DocsDetailsDialog`. Thoughts?
author: shssoichiro

body:
Ah yes it was originally for debugging so you could see what was being indexed, since e.g. the CheerioCrawler has odd indexing output for some sites with h3 headers, etc.

Now I understand it's more of a feature to be able to click the links. Could we either re-add a little eye icon to a docs status that opens the docs details dialog for debugging, or fully clean it up by removing `getDetails` message/function/types/etc before merging this?
author: RomneyDa

body: Since we have the code in place already, it does seem useful to be able to use the existing dialog for debugging. I'll add an icon to allow opening it. Thanks.
author: shssoichiro

body: I've added in the icon to display the dialog. Since we are restricted to the sidepane area, it unfortunately leaves the dialog a bit cramped, but the sidepan can be expanded if needed. The alternative would be to rewrite the docs dialog as text/markdown to display in a virtual file tab, but that wasn't much prettier, so I took the path of using the existing component.
author: shssoichiro

body: Thanks, added.

body:
@RomneyDa 
Due to this: [preserveReasoning](https://openrouter.ai/docs/use-cases/reasoning-tokens#preserving-reasoning-blocks), I added preserveReasoning option.

The previous behaviour was to strip all the reasoning, but it seems to be a bad idea for many cases when tools are used.

In most cases models ignore the thinking blocks, but some may use them, for example GPT-5 returns an encrypted thinking block at the end, that I suspect will be used in some cases. In some special cases (e.g. switching models in the same conversation), they may cause problems. Now I made the default behavior to preserve the thinking blocks in the openai compatible endpoints, but this behavior can be disabled by setting preserveReasoning to false. Please let me know if it's OK, or if you have any other suggestions.

Thanks for the feedback\! You were absolutely right - the original implementation was too extensive and didn't integrate cleanly with the existing reasoning system.

## What I changed to address your feedback:

**✅ Integrated with existing `<think>` tag system** instead of creating parallel logic:
- OpenAI's `reasoning` field now gets converted to `<think>` tag format 
- This allows it to flow through the same well-tested reasoning handling code
- Much cleaner integration with minimal new code in `streamUpdate`
- Added `isOpenAIReasoning` field to differentiate reasoning sources for correct ending behavior
- `<think>` tags only end with explicit `</think>` 
- OpenAI reasoning field ends when content appears without reasoning field

**✅ Following Ollama's harmony approach**:
- Researched how Ollama handles OpenAI reasoning field in their harmony implementation
- Treats reasoning as separate streaming content that doesn't interfere with main content flow
- Maintains the user-facing experience Continue users expect

**Result**: All 272 tests now pass (100% pass rate) with a much cleaner, more maintainable implementation that properly integrates with existing systems instead of duplicating logic.

<!-- continue-cli-review -->
## Code Review Summary

### ✅ Strengths
- **Clear structure**: Well-organized workflow with logical step progression and clear naming conventions
- **Comprehensive security**: Proper permissions scope (read-only contents, write for PR comments)
- **Good error handling**: Uses conditional checks, artifact uploads, and try-catch blocks for robustness
- **Artifact management**: Properly uploads review results with appropriate retention policy
- **Comment management**: Smart logic to update existing bot comments instead of creating duplicates
- **Environment isolation**: Uses proper environment variable handling for secrets

### ⚠️ Issues Found

**HIGH SEVERITY:**
- **Hardcoded CLI version**: Line 28 pins to a specific version `@continuedev/cli@1.4.25` which will become outdated and may introduce compatibility issues
- **Missing error handling**: The `gh pr diff` command (line 34) and Continue CLI execution (line 88) lack proper error handling if they fail

**MEDIUM SEVERITY:**
- **Workflow trigger scope**: Triggers on `pull_request.opened` and `ready_for_review` but misses subsequent pushes to PR branches, meaning code changes won't trigger re-reviews
- **Resource usage**: `fetch-depth: 0` fetches entire git history which may be unnecessary for PR diffs and could impact performance
- **Inconsistent condition**: The workflow only runs when `github.event.pull_request.draft == false` but doesn't check this in the trigger conditions

**LOW SEVERITY:**
- **Magic strings**: Bot signature `<!-- continue-cli-review -->` could be defined as a constant
- **Hardcoded organization**: Uses `continuedev` org and `review-bot` config without making them configurable

### 💡 Suggestions

1. **Make CLI version configurable**: Use a workflow input or environment variable for the CLI version instead of hardcoding
2. **Add comprehensive triggers**: Include `synchronize` event to re-review when PR is updated:
   ```yaml
   on:
     pull_request:
       types: [opened, ready_for_review, synchronize]
   ```
3. **Add error handling**: Wrap critical commands in conditional checks:
   ```bash
   if ! gh pr diff ${{ github.event.number }} > pr_diff.txt; then
     echo "Failed to get PR diff" && exit 1
   fi
   ```
4. **Optimize git fetch**: Use `fetch-depth: 1` unless full history is specifically needed
5. **Add workflow inputs**: Make organization and config configurable for reusability
6. **Consider rate limiting**: Add logic to prevent excessive API calls for rapid PR updates

### 🚀 Overall Assessment

**COMMENT** - The workflow is well-structured and functional but has several areas for improvement, particularly around error handling and version management. The security implementation is solid, and the overall approach is sound. The issues found are not critical enough to block deployment but should be addressed to ensure long-term maintainability and reliability.

## Code Review Summary

### ✅ Strengths
- **Clear Documentation**: Good addition to PR template explaining the AI review feature and how to trigger it
- **Comprehensive Workflows**: Both workflows handle multiple trigger scenarios (PR events and comments)
- **Permission Controls**: Proper access controls limiting AI reviews to team members only (OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR)
- **Error Handling**: Good fallback mechanisms when review creation fails
- **Artifact Management**: Proper uploading of review artifacts with appropriate retention periods

### ⚠️ Issues Found

#### High
- **Inconsistent CLI Versions**: The two workflows use different Continue CLI versions (`@latest` vs `@1.4.25`), which could lead to inconsistent behavior and unpredictable results
- **Missing Secret Documentation**: The workflows reference `CONTINUE_API_KEY` secret but there's no documentation about how to set this up or what permissions it needs
- **Hardcoded Configuration**: Both workflows use hardcoded `--org continuedev --config continuedev/review-bot` which may not work for all repositories or deployments

#### Medium
- **Duplicate Workflow Logic**: Both workflows share similar setup steps and permission checks - this could be refactored into a reusable action to reduce maintenance overhead
- **Missing Validation**: No validation that the PR diff was successfully retrieved before passing it to the AI review
- **Large Prompt Risk**: The inline review workflow could generate very large prompts with extensive diffs, potentially hitting API limits

#### Low
- **Trigger Comment Mismatch**: PR template mentions `@continue-review` but inline workflow expects `@continue-inline-review` - this inconsistency could confuse users
- **Missing Timeout Configuration**: While workflows have 10-minute timeouts, there's no timeout specified for the Continue CLI command itself

### 💡 Suggestions
- **Unify CLI Versions**: Use the same Continue CLI version across both workflows or add a comment explaining why different versions are needed
- **Add Setup Documentation**: Include documentation about required secrets and configuration setup
- **Extract Common Logic**: Consider creating a composite action for shared setup and permission checking logic
- **Add Diff Size Limits**: Consider adding checks for maximum diff size to prevent API issues
- **Improve Error Messages**: Add more descriptive error messages when reviews fail to help with debugging

### 🚀 Overall Assessment
COMMENT - The implementation is solid and well-structured, but needs some refinements around consistency and documentation before merging. The security controls are appropriate and the feature will provide valuable automation for the team.

- **Comprehensive Implementation**: Both general review and inline review workflows are well-structured with clear separation of concerns
- **Security Model**: Proper permission restrictions limiting execution to team members only (OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR)

- **Hardcoded Configuration**: Both workflows use hardcoded `--org continuedev --config continuedev/review-bot` parameters without making them configurable

#### Medium
- **Timeout Management**: While both workflows have 10-minute timeouts, there's no graceful handling of timeout scenarios or partial results
- **Resource Usage**: The inline review workflow fetches full git history (`fetch-depth: 0`) but may not need it, potentially slowing down execution
- **Comment Collision**: No mechanism to prevent multiple review comments if the workflow is triggered multiple times quickly

#### Low
- **Missing Input Validation**: No validation that the PR actually contains code changes worth reviewing
- **Limited Feedback**: The workflows don't provide progress indicators or intermediate status updates during execution
- **Artifact Retention**: Different retention periods (7 vs 30 days) between similar workflows without clear justification

- **Centralize Configuration**: Extract the Continue CLI version, organization, and config to workflow variables or inputs for easier maintenance
- **Add Conditional Logic**: Consider skipping reviews for documentation-only changes or very small PRs to reduce noise
- **Implement Rate Limiting**: Add checks to prevent excessive API usage if multiple PRs are opened simultaneously
- **Enhance Error Messages**: Provide more descriptive error messages in the fallback scenarios to help users understand what went wrong
- **Add Workflow Status**: Consider adding workflow status badges or notifications to help track review completion

**COMMENT** - This is a solid implementation of AI-powered code review functionality with good security practices and error handling. ## Code Review Summary

### ✅ Strengths
- **Architecture**: The implementation follows a well-structured pattern with proper separation of concerns between the PrefetchQueue, NextEditProvider, and protocol layers
- **Singleton Pattern**: Good use of singleton pattern for both PrefetchQueue and NextEditProvider, ensuring single instances throughout the application
- **Error Handling**: Comprehensive error handling with try-catch blocks and proper abort signal management
- **Logging**: Extensive console logging for debugging purposes throughout the new functionality

### ⚠️ Issues Found

#### High
- **Excessive Console Logging**: The code contains numerous console.log statements that should not be in production code. These will clutter logs and potentially impact performance.

#### Medium
- **Missing Type Safety**: The `processOne` method in PrefetchQueue accepts `ctx: any`, which bypasses TypeScript's type checking. This should use proper typing from the AutocompleteInput interface.

- **State Management Concerns**: The PrefetchQueue maintains both `unprocessedQueue` and `processedQueue` arrays but doesn't have clear lifecycle management or memory limits. This could lead to memory issues with large queues.

- **Missing Error Recovery**: While there's error handling in the process loop, there's no mechanism to retry failed items or notify the caller about failures.

#### Low
- **Inconsistent Property Access**: In `NextEditPrefetchQueue`, the `usingFullFileDiff` property is initialized but never properly set through the unused `initialize` method.

- **Commented Code**: There are several blocks of commented-out code that should be removed if no longer needed (e.g., in `NextEditProvider.ts` lines 577-578).

- **Magic Numbers**: The default prefetch limit of 3 is hardcoded without explanation of why this value was chosen.

### 💡 Suggestions

- **Add Proper TypeScript Types**: Define a proper interface for the `ctx` parameter in `processOne` to ensure type safety:
  ```typescript
  interface ProcessContext extends Omit<AutocompleteInput, 'pos' | 'filepath'> {
    // additional fields if needed
  }
  ```

- **Implement Queue Size Limits**: Add maximum queue size limits to prevent unbounded memory growth:
  ```typescript
  private readonly MAX_QUEUE_SIZE = 100;
  
  enqueueUnprocessed(location: RangeInFile): void {
    if (this.unprocessedQueue.length >= this.MAX_QUEUE_SIZE) {
      this.unprocessedQueue.shift(); // Remove oldest
    }
    this.unprocessedQueue.push(location);
  }
  ```

- **Add Metrics/Monitoring**: Consider adding proper metrics instead of console.logs for production monitoring:
  ```typescript
  private metrics = {
    processed: 0,
    failed: 0,
    aborted: 0
  };
  ```

- **Implement Proper Initialization**: Either use the `initialize` method or remove it:
  ```typescript
  constructor(prefetchLimit: number = 3, usingFullFileDiff: boolean = true) {
    this.prefetchLimit = prefetchLimit;
    this.usingFullFileDiff = usingFullFileDiff;
    this.abortController = new AbortController();
  }
  ```

- **Add Unit Tests**: No tests are included for the new PrefetchQueue functionality. Consider adding tests for queue operations, abort behavior, and edge cases.

### 🚀 Overall Assessment
**REQUEST_CHANGES**

The implementation adds valuable prefetching functionality to the NextEdit feature, but requires cleanup before merging. The main concerns are:
1. Remove all console.log statements or replace with proper logging
2. Fix the type safety issue with the `any` type in processOne
3. Consider adding memory management for the queues
4. Add proper initialization or remove the unused method

The architecture is sound and the feature appears well-integrated with the existing codebase, but these issues should be addressed to maintain code quality and prevent potential production issues.

## Code Review Summary

### ✅ Strengths
- **Security-conscious approach**: The PR addresses a real security concern by preserving telemetry preferences even when the global context file is corrupted
- **Comprehensive test coverage**: The test suite includes 6 new test cases covering various edge cases, including different salvage scenarios and malformed data
- **Graceful error handling**: The implementation doesn't crash when encountering corrupted data and attempts to preserve as much information as possible
- **Proper use of existing infrastructure**: The code reuses the existing `salvageSharedConfig` function from `sharedConfig.ts` for consistency
- **Documentation improvements**: The Azure documentation updates clarify important configuration details

### ⚠️ Issues Found

#### Medium
- **Regex-based JSON parsing**: The salvage implementation uses regex to extract JSON objects (`/"sharedConfig"\s*:\s*({[^}]*})/`), which is fragile and may fail for nested objects or strings containing `}`. For example, if `sharedConfig` contains nested objects or string values with braces, the regex will fail to capture the complete object.

- **Limited salvage scope**: The current implementation only attempts to salvage `allowAnonymousTelemetry` from `sharedConfig`, but the existing `salvageSharedConfig` function supports salvaging additional security-sensitive fields like `disableIndexing`, `disableSessionTitles`, and `disableAutocompleteInFiles`. The custom salvage logic should leverage all of these.

#### Low
- **Code duplication**: The salvage logic in `GlobalContext.ts` duplicates some of the validation logic already present in `salvageSharedConfig`. This creates maintenance overhead and potential for inconsistencies.

- **Incomplete error context**: The catch blocks use empty catch statements without logging the actual error, which could make debugging difficult.

### 💡 Suggestions
- **Leverage existing salvage function**: Instead of implementing custom regex parsing, consider parsing the entire file more robustly or directly calling the existing `salvageSharedConfig` function with partially parsed data.

- **More robust JSON extraction**: If regex parsing is necessary, consider using a more sophisticated approach that handles nested objects, or use a JSON streaming parser that can handle partial/corrupted JSON.

- **Add logging for debugging**: Add error logging in catch blocks to help with debugging when salvage operations fail.

- **Consider salvaging all top-level fields**: The current implementation only salvages `sharedConfig`, but other fields like `indexingPaused`, `hasAlreadyCreatedAPromptFile`, etc., could also be preserved.

### 🚀 Overall Assessment
**APPROVE**

This is a well-intentioned change that improves the robustness of the application by preserving user privacy preferences even when configuration files become corrupted. While there are some implementation details that could be improved, the core functionality works correctly and the comprehensive test coverage ensures the feature behaves as expected. The issues identified are not critical and can be addressed in follow-up PRs if needed.

- **Debug Logging in Production**: Extensive `println` statements throughout the code that should be replaced with proper logging framework
  - Found in `NextEditWindowManager`, `ContinueInlineCompletionProvider`, and other classes
  - These will pollute console output in production

- **EDT Threading Issues**: Potential EDT (Event Dispatch Thread) violations in `getModelTitles()` function
  - Uses `runBlocking` on EDT which can freeze the UI
  - Comment acknowledges this is a known issue but still problematic

#### Medium
- **Resource Management**: Missing proper cleanup for coroutines and listeners
  - `NextEditWindowManager` registers selection change handlers but no clear unregistration
  - Potential memory leaks if popups aren't properly disposed

- **Error Handling**: Inconsistent error handling patterns
  - Some methods swallow exceptions silently
  - `parseNextEditOutcome` catches all exceptions but only logs to console

- **Hardcoded Values**: Several magic numbers and hardcoded timeouts
  - `MAX_MODEL_WAIT_TIME = 1500`
  - Various pixel offsets and dimensions in UI code

#### Low
- **Code Organization**: Some very large methods that could be refactored
  - `showNextEditWindow` method is 90+ lines
  - `acceptEdit` method has deep nesting and multiple responsibilities

- **State Management**: Using mutable instance variables for state tracking
  - `lastUuid`, `lastProject`, `isUsingNextEdit` in `ContinueInlineCompletionProvider`
  - Comment acknowledges this is a hack but still problematic

### 💡 Suggestions
- **Logging Framework**: Replace all `println` statements with proper logging using IntelliJ's Logger
  ```kotlin
  private val LOG = Logger.getInstance(NextEditWindowManager::class.java)
  LOG.debug("showNextEditWindow called with...")
  ```

- **Configuration**: Extract hardcoded values to configuration
  ```kotlin
  object NextEditConfig {
      const val DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000
      const val MODEL_WAIT_TIME_MS = 1500
  }
  ```

- **Async Improvements**: Replace `runBlocking` with proper async handling
  ```kotlin
  suspend fun getModelTitles(project: Project): List<String> {
      return withTimeoutOrNull(MAX_MODEL_WAIT_TIME.milliseconds) {
          // ... existing logic
      } ?: emptyList()
  }
  ```

- **Method Extraction**: Break down large methods into smaller, focused ones
  - Extract popup creation logic from `showNextEditWindow`
  - Separate validation from execution in `acceptEdit`

### 🚀 Overall Assessment
**REQUEST_CHANGES**

This PR represents a significant architectural improvement by adopting IntelliJ's native inline completion API. The implementation is generally solid with good async patterns and service abstractions. However, the extensive debug logging and EDT blocking issues need to be addressed before merging to production. The code would also benefit from better error handling and resource management patterns.

The Next Edit feature is a sophisticated addition that appears well-thought-out, but the implementation complexity suggests it would benefit from additional refactoring to improve maintainability.

body:
> Neat idea! I think we should add them as experimental tools to begin with so we can play around with them a bit before shipping to all users.
> 
> How does the model know how many lines to read at the beginning of a file, or the range?
> 
> In general, curious what your inspiration here was - any particular behavioral patterns you've noticed that led you to think that these tools would be helpful?

@Patrick-Erichsen inspired by a use case to process large files including logs. These files might have headers in the first row, and row sampling can help the LLM discover format quickly and then create strategies to process log data. These strategies might involve hte development of python, or terminal usage to process the logs in bulk. With the addition of parallel tool calls processing multiple log files can be done quickly. For example, you can ask for the LLM to take mutliple log files, sample the first 50 lines and look for anomolies in server startup times, or errors.

I'd be happy to introduce them as experimental. Could you perhaps point me to a resource I can look at to add the specific flags? I'd also be happy to add this to the contributing guide as a strategy to add new tools if that helps! Thanks for the awesome question.
